intro_md: 🎧 **12 min.** Episode 4, part 2 – the story goes on **on the tram**. This is new listening (not the same as the reading). Learn 4 chunks, then listen with the words hidden.

parts.title: Hope Street – Episode 4 (2/2): On the tram
parts.md:
![On the tram](data/img/w1/d14-tram.webp)

**Four chunks for the tram:**

| Phrase | 🖼️ Picture it (literal) | So it means… |
|---|---|---|
| *tap your card* | Your hand touches a small machine with a card – one quick **tap**, like a knock. | pay by touching your card on a reader – *"You can tap your phone at the café too."* |
| *get off at* | You are **on** the bus, then you step **off** it at a place. | leave the bus/tram at a certain stop – *"Please get off at the third stop."* |
| *the next stop* | The bus is moving; the very next place where it stands still. | the following place where it stops – *"The next stop is the station."* |
| *the wrong way* | An arrow points left, but your feet go right. | in the opposite direction from the right one – *"We drove the wrong way and got lost."* |

**Train your ears – the words are hidden at first:**
1. 👂 **Listen without the words.** Just follow. Missed a word? Keep going – the next sentence often explains it.
2. 👂 **Listen again**, still without the words. You'll catch more.
3. 📄 **Show transcript** – listen + read. **Tap any line** you missed to hear just that part again.
4. 👂 **Hide it** and listen one last time.

listen.text: The tram arrived, and Margaret and Nam climbed on.
Where do I buy a ticket?
You don't need a paper one, dear. Just tap your card on the reader, like this.
Nam tapped his bank card. The reader beeped, and a green light came on.
That's so easy! At home, I have to queue for ten minutes.
Now, listen. We get off at St Peter's Square.
Is this our stop?
No, not yet. The next stop is ours.
Two stops later, a man in a dark blue jacket walked down the tram.
Tickets, please, everyone. Have your tickets ready.
Here you go. I tapped my card when I got on.
That's fine, thank you, sir. Enjoy your day.
Phew. I'm so glad I tapped it.
Don't worry. But I'll tell you a secret – I once went the wrong way on a tram.
Really? What happened?
It was 1985. I was on holiday in Blackpool, and I wanted to see the sea.
I got on the first tram I saw, and I sat down very happily.
Twenty minutes later, I was in a car park, miles from the sea!
Oh no! What did you do?
I waited for the next tram, and I went back the right way. I was very late for my tea.
The tram stopped, and they stepped out into the bright square.
Here we are. I'm going to buy some flowers. Where will you go?
I'll try to find the Saturday market. Thank you for everything, Margaret.
Enjoy yourself, dear. And mind the bikes!
